'''''Centaurea melitensis''''' (called '''Maltese star-thistle'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref>{{PLANTS|id=CEME2|taxon=Centaurea melitensis|accessdate=13 January 2016}}</ref> in Europe, '''tocalote''' or '''tocolote''' in western North America) is an [[annual plant]] in the family Asteraceae, {{convert|1|to|11|dm|0}} high, with resin-dotted leaves and spine-tipped phyllaries. This plant is native to the Mediterranean region of Europe and Africa. It was introduced to North America in the 18th century; the first documented occurrence in California is in the adobe of a building constructed in [[San Fernando, California|San Fernando]] in 1797. It is also naturalized on a number of Pacific islands.

==Conservation==
It is considered rare on the [[Maltese Islands]], being listed in the Red Data Book.<ref name=maltese>{{cite web | url = http://www.maltawildplants.com/ASTR/Centaurea_melitensis.php | title = Centaurea melitensis   (Maltese Star-Thistle). | website = maltawildplants.com | access-date = 4 September 2021 | year = 2020}}</ref>
